title: Greg Joswiak Announces In-Store iPhone Duo Availability, Forecasts Strong Demand Pre‑Launch
body:
Apple’s newest flagship, the iPhone 15 Duo, is set to hit retail shelves today, and the company’s senior vice‑president of worldwide marketing, Greg Joswiak, says Apple is preparing for a surge of in‑store demand after a chaotic pre‑order period. The tech giant has reportedly stocked its global network of Apple Stores with a “significant” inventory of the dual‑camera, dual‑processor device, aiming to smooth out the frustrations that many customers experienced when trying to secure a unit online. Joswiak’s comments, delivered in an exclusive interview with a leading tech outlet, underline Apple’s confidence that the Duo will quickly become one of its best‑selling models this year.

The pre‑order phase for the iPhone 15 Duo was marked by server overloads, long queue times and a slew of reports about customers being unable to complete purchases. While Apple’s e‑commerce platform eventually stabilized, the hiccups sparked a wave of criticism on social media, prompting the company to pivot toward a stronger in‑store rollout. “We’ve learned a lot from the launch experience,” Joswiak said. “Our goal is to make the Duo readily available to anyone who walks into an Apple Store, whether they’re a longtime fan or a first‑time buyer.” He added that the company has increased staffing levels at its most trafficked locations and is offering same‑day pickup for customers who place orders online but prefer to collect the device in person.

Analysts see Apple’s emphasis on brick‑and‑mortar availability as a strategic move to protect brand perception and capture revenue that might otherwise be lost to competitors. The iPhone 15 Duo, featuring a novel dual‑camera system that combines a 48‑megapixel main sensor with a 12‑megapixel ultra‑wide lens, is positioned as a premium offering that could command higher average selling prices. By ensuring that stores are well‑stocked, Apple hopes to reduce the “scarcity” narrative that can drive customers toward the secondary market, where resale prices often exceed retail and erode Apple’s margin expectations. Moreover, in‑store experiences provide an additional sales channel for accessories, AppleCare plans and trade‑in offers, further boosting the overall transaction value.

The rollout strategy also reflects Apple’s broader supply‑chain resilience efforts. After a series of disruptions caused by component shortages and geopolitical tensions, the company has reportedly secured a larger allocation of the new A17 Bionic chips that power the Duo. This inventory cushion allows Apple to meet the anticipated demand spikes in key markets such as the United States, Europe and China, where early adopters are expected to line up outside stores before opening hours. Retail managers have confirmed that many locations are extending operating hours and designating dedicated “Duo” sections to streamline the checkout process and minimize wait times.

Consumer sentiment appears cautiously optimistic. Early reviews of the iPhone 15 Duo highlight its refined design, improved battery life and the seamless integration of iOS 17’s new features, such as advanced photo‑editing tools and AI‑driven widgets. However, price sensitivity remains a factor; the Duo’s starting price sits several hundred dollars above the base iPhone 15 model, prompting some shoppers to weigh the benefits of the upgraded hardware against the cost. Apple’s financing options, including monthly installment plans and trade‑in credits, are expected to play a pivotal role in converting interest into sales, especially among younger demographics.

Looking ahead, the success of today’s in‑store launch could set a precedent for how Apple manages future product releases. If the Duo’s retail performance meets or exceeds expectations, the company may double down on physical‑store inventory strategies for upcoming devices, potentially reshaping the balance between online and offline sales channels. For now, Apple’s leadership is watching the opening day closely, ready to adjust supply allocations in real time. As queues form and devices begin to leave the shelves, the iPhone 15 Duo’s market reception will offer a clear gauge of consumer appetite for Apple’s latest innovations and the effectiveness of its revised distribution approach.
